name: Battle of Asculum
intro: Near Asculum in Apulia, the year after Heraclea. You are the consuls Publius Decius Mus and Publius Sulpicius Saverrio, with four legions and allies, about 70,000 foot and 8,000 horse by one ancient count (another gives 40,000 a side). King Pyrrhus of Epirus has about as many men, a phalanx and 19 elephants.
debrief: In reality, the accounts differ. In the main one, the first day’s fighting was on rough, wooded ground near the river, where Pyrrhus could not use his elephants and cavalry, and night ended it. Pyrrhus then occupied the broken ground in the night and forced a battle on the plain, charging with archers and slingers among his elephants, and drove the Romans back to their camp. Another account describes the Romans’ 300 anti-elephant wagons stopping the elephants until light troops attacked their crews, and Daunian allies burning Pyrrhus’s camp; a third claims a Roman victory. Losses are given as 6,000 Roman and 3,505 Epirote. Pyrrhus is said to have remarked that one more such victory would ruin him, the origin of the phrase ‘Pyrrhic victory’. Holding the broken ground, screening the wagons and counter-attacking are what-ifs.

win: Asculum is a Roman victory after all.
lose: The elephants drive you to your camp.
‘One more victory like this and we are lost.’

decisions.title: Rough ground
decisions.text: Pyrrhus has crossed into Apulia. The first day’s fighting comes on rough, wooded ground near the river, where his elephants and cavalry cannot deploy.

hint.text: The broken ground hampers the phalanx and the elephants.

scout.text: On this ground the legions’ flexibility counts and Pyrrhus’s strengths do not. Fight here and hold it.

choices.label: Fight on the broken ground by the river

fx.text: The legions fight hard among the trees and gullies. The elephants cannot come up. Night ends the fighting with nothing decided.

choices.label: Come out onto the open plain where your legions can form

fx.text: On the plain the elephants and cavalry have room.

decisions.title: Pyrrhus moves by night
decisions.text: In the night Pyrrhus sends a detachment to occupy the broken ground, so that tomorrow the battle must be fought on the plain.

hint.text: Your scouts hear men moving on the rough ground.

scout.text: If your own troops hold the broken ground tonight, Pyrrhus cannot force the battle onto the plain.

choices.label: Do nothing; fight on the plain tomorrow

fx.text: At dawn the broken ground is in Pyrrhus’s hands, and you must fight on open ground.

choices.label: Send cohorts by night to hold the broken ground

fx.text: Your cohorts reach the gullies first. In the morning Pyrrhus still faces rough ground.

choices.label: Withdraw to camp and refuse battle on his chosen ground

decisions.title: The wagons
decisions.text: You have built 300 wagons against the elephants: swinging poles tipped with spikes, scythes and grapnels, fire pots, and crews of archers and slingers.

hint.text: Pyrrhus has light troops posted among his elephants.

scout.text: The wagons can stop the elephants, but their crews are exposed. Screen them with velites and javelin men, or Pyrrhus’s light troops will pick them off.

choices.label: Put the wagons in front, crews ready at the poles

fx.text: The wagons stop the elephants at first, but Pyrrhus’s light troops cut down the crews, who flee back into the legions.
The wagons hold the elephants back.

choices.label: Put the wagons in front, velites guarding them

fx.text: Velites and javelin men keep Pyrrhus’s light troops off the wagon crews. Spikes and fire turn the elephants back.
Nothing stands between the elephants and the legions.

decisions.title: The elephants charge
decisions.text: Pyrrhus charges in close order, with archers and slingers between the elephants. Your line must face it head-on.

hint.text: The elephants are coming straight at the centre.

scout.text: Elephants are terrible head-on. Open lanes, let them through, and attack them from the sides.

choices.label: Stand firm and meet them head-on with pila

fx.text: The wagons blunt the charge, but the line is pushed back.
The elephants smash into the legions and drive them back toward the camp.

choices.label: Open lanes and hit the elephants from the sides

fx.text: The maniples open lanes. The elephants pour through and are speared from both sides.
You lose the field, but keep the army.

decisions.title: Smoke over Pyrrhus’s camp
decisions.text: Smoke rises behind the enemy. A force of Daunian allies has stumbled on Pyrrhus’s camp and set it alight. Pyrrhus himself has been wounded.

hint.text: Pyrrhus is sending his elephants and best horse back to the camp.

scout.text: His army is split and its king is hurt. A counter-attack now could turn the day.

choices.label: Pull back to your own camp

fx.text: Your army withdraws. Both sides spend the night counting their losses.

choices.label: Counter-attack while his best troops ride back

fx.text: As the elephants and horse ride back to the burning camp, your legions charge the phalanx. Pyrrhus’s line breaks.

choices.label: Send the cavalry to help the Daunians finish the camp

fx.text: The cavalry reaches the camp, but the main battle is left alone.

quotes.text: If we are victorious in one more battle with the Romans, we shall be utterly ruined.
quotes.who: Pyrrhus, to a man who congratulated him
